subject: Computer Networking
title: Lazy Loading
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lazy Loading.

hook.text: A page has 50 images but only 3 are visible. Why load all 50? Lazy loading defers the rest until needed.

buildup.text: The loading='lazy' attribute on tells the browser to load images only when they enter the viewport.

discovery.text: Intersection Observer API gives precise control. Trigger loads when elements are N pixels from view.

twist.text: Lazy load too aggressively and above-the-fold images appear blank. Exempt hero images from lazy loading.

climax.text: Code splitting lazy-loads JavaScript too. Import components only when the user navigates to them.

punchline.text: Load what's visible. Defer the rest. Faster for everyone.

quiz.question: What HTML attribute enables native lazy loading for images?

details.summary: Lazy loading defers downloading of offscreen resources until the user scrolls near them. Native browser lazy loading uses the loading=lazy attribute on images and iframes. For JavaScript modules, dynamic import() loads code only when needed.
details.whyItMatters: Users rarely scroll through an entire page immediately. Lazy loading avoids wasting bandwidth and processing time on content the user may never see, dramatically improving initial load.
takeaways: loading=lazy on images defers downloading until near the viewport
Dynamic import() loads JavaScript modules on demand
Initial page weight drops significantly on long content pages

faq.question: Should all images use lazy loading?
faq.answer: No. Images visible in the initial viewport should load eagerly because lazy loading them could delay LCP. Apply lazy loading only to images below the fold that users must scroll to see. The first visible image should use loading=eager or simply omit the attribute for default eager behavior.

faq.question: What is code splitting?
faq.answer: Code splitting breaks JavaScript bundles into smaller chunks loaded on demand. Only the code needed for the current page ships initially. Additional code loads when the user navigates or triggers features.
